turns.text:
ok so i heard a girl in the hallway today gushing about how ms tolentino's class is the best one she's ever taken. genuinely i think grace's students like her more than i do lol. anyway. be brutal, does this message work

"Mom. I know you think the SAT plan is me being dramatic, but wow, shocking, your daughter who has never once been late on a deadline has a plan. Harper runs free prep at the library every Saturday and I do two practice sections a week on my own. I don't need a lecture about how a 'real' schedule works, I need you to stop acting like I'm making this up. Can you just actually listen for once"

The plan itself is solid and specific, which is your strongest asset. The problem is the framing. The sarcasm and the "for once" will make her react to your tone instead of your plan. Here's a version that keeps your voice but gives her less to push back on:

"Mom, I want to walk you through my SAT plan, because I think it's a good one. Harper runs free prep sessions at the library every Saturday, and on my own I do two timed practice sections a week. I'd like to show you how I'm tracking my scores so you can see it's working. Can we sit down for ten minutes this weekend?"

If you want it to land harder, add one line with your most recent practice score so she has something concrete to react to. Want a version that's a bit shorter or a bit more casual?
ok thats actually better. add the score thing, i missed 3 on math last time so maybe dont lead with that lol. also its past midnight and i have a 6:50 alarm so im gonna send it tomorrow

Smart to hold it until morning. Messages sent when you're tired tend to read sharper than you mean them to. Here's the version with a score line that doesn't lead with the weak spot:

"Mom, I want to walk you through my SAT plan, because I think it's a good one. Harper runs free prep sessions at the library every Saturday, and on my own I do two timed practice sections a week. My reading scores on those have been solid, and I'm using the math misses to decide what to drill next. Can we sit down for ten minutes this weekend so I can show you how I'm tracking it?"

That frames the math misses as part of the plan rather than a problem. Good luck with it.
